headline: Hy Memory 2.0: Tencent's Open-Source Model That Only Remembers
summary: Tencent's Hy Memory 2.0, released October 15, 2026, is an open-source stack designed to manage AI agent memory, allowing larger models to focus on core tasks. It offers a tiny inference footprint and integrates seamlessly with existing memory systems.
details: AI agents often forget preferences and instructions after a session. Tencent's Hy Memory 2.0, an open-source stack released October 15, 2026, is designed to manage this memory, allowing larger AI models to focus their processing power on core tasks instead of remembering.

Tencent reports a 55.49% macro average across memory benchmarks, showing parity with Claude Opus 5's 54.62%. While these are internal benchmarks, the open-source license and tiny inference footprint are confirmed, offering a unique specialist solution.

Hy Memory 2.0 integrates seamlessly into existing memory systems like Mem0 or MemOS as a memory-writer. This allows users to drop the model in without altering their current storage or retrieval infrastructure. A 3B-active specialist handles bookkeeping, freeing up frontier models to focus on complex reasoning.

This release continues a trend of unbundling monolithic AI models, following DeepSeek's V4.1-Flash for speed and Meta's Muse Wonder for memory and focus. Tencent's contribution further specializes AI agent components, enhancing efficiency and modularity in the ecosystem.

headline: Oura sues rival Ultrahuman again, threatening its U.S. smart ring comeback
summary: Smart ring maker Oura has filed a new lawsuit against Ultrahuman, seeking to block U.S. sales of its Ring Pro and claiming infringement of two patents, one issued just days before the filing. This reignites a legal battle that previously led to an import ban o
details: Smart ring maker Oura has sued Indian rival Ultrahuman again, seeking to block U.S. sales of its Ring Pro and monetary damages. Oura alleges the Ring Pro infringes two of its patents covering the ring’s design and internal components, including its battery and sensors. One of these patents was issued just two days before the lawsuit was filed.

This case follows an import ban on Ultrahuman’s earlier Ring Air, which took effect last year after Oura secured a patent infringement ruling from the International Trade Commission. Ultrahuman's redesigned Ring Pro had only recently received a favorable ruling from U.S. Customs and Border Protection, allowing its return to the American market.

An Oura spokesperson stated that Ultrahuman "has a history of copying Oura’s innovations" and failed to address continued infringement with the redesigned ring. Oura claims Ultrahuman is attempting to capitalize on Oura's innovation and market leadership.

Oura argues that the U.S. Customs ruling only covered the patent involved in the earlier dispute, not the two patents cited in its latest lawsuit: D804,471 and 12,769,363. The company stated it is "forced to file this complaint of patent infringement" to protect its rights.

The lawsuit also names Texas-based electronics manufacturer SVTronics as a defendant, alleging it manufactures the Ring Pro under Ultrahuman’s direction. Both companies are accused of infringing Oura’s patents through the manufacture, importation, and sale of the device in the U.S.

Oura has a history of pursuing patent infringement claims against other smart ring makers, including Samsung, RingConn, Circular, and Zepp Health. Some of these disputes have resulted in licensing agreements, with companies like RingConn and Circular agreeing to pay royalties.

This legal battle unfolds as the smart-ring market continues to expand, with research firm IDC projecting global shipments to grow 12.8% this year to 4.9 million units. While Oura remains a leader, Ultrahuman is among the growing competitors in the category.

The lawsuit comes weeks after Oura shelved its $2.2 billion IPO, citing market uncertainty, and months after Ultrahuman raised $70 million. Ultrahuman is also collaborating with Qualcomm on a new smart ring to expand into AI interactions and gaming.
